gap_list: Tieback distance, all ten records: no primary source states a well, cluster or drill-centre distance to host. Needs OTC/SPE paper text or regulator pipeline-segment data, neither reachable here.
Manifold/PLEM/PLET count: missing for eight of ten (all but Stones and Lucius). Contractor releases for Appomattox and Mad Dog Phase 2 name manifolds without counts.
Tree count as such: stated only for Stones and Lucius. Elsewhere only well counts are stated, and wells are not trees.

Project cost with year and scope: no primary statement for any record. Mad Dog Phase 2 has a secondary report of the operator figure; Appomattox and Whale operators published percentages and a rate of return, not costs.
Regulator data (BSEE/BOEM water depths, structure and pipeline records): not read, PDF and interactive-query formats only.
Paper abstracts (OTC/SPE/JPT) for Perdido, Stones, Na Kika, Thunder Horse: blocked.

Operator originals for all Shell and bp releases: wire copies were used for Shell; nothing for bp. The Appomattox FID quotes (rows 17 to 25, source S4) come from a third-party reproduction and should be re-checked against the original.
Whale umbilical and drill-center sentences (rows 12, 13) need a verbatim re-capture from S3.
recommendation: Keep the parent data-backfill issue open and keep the downstream benchmark issue on `status:needs-data`: fewer than 10 records pass (0 pass all four fields; 2 pass trees plus manifolds at contractor-scope level). Two decisions would change what is achievable: whether contractor award scope counts as an accepted source for tree and manifold counts (as-contracted, not as-built), and whether the gate should require `tieback_distance_km` at all given no public primary statement was found for any of the ten. A follow-up pass from a host that can read PDFs and reach OnePetro and regulator data would close gaps 1, 5 and 6 fastest.
